name: studio
//optionalDependencies: Native binaries for platforms other than the one that generated the lockfile.
npm records an optional dependency only for the platform it resolved on, so a
package-lock.json generated on Linux has lightningcss-linux-x64-gnu and no
win32 entry at all. `npm install` on Windows then never fetches the binary and
Tailwind dies at the first CSS import with 'Cannot find module
--os=win32` does not fix it — it prunes rather than adds.
Declaring them here forces every variant into the lockfile. They stay optional,
and each one carries its own os/cpu constraints, so npm still installs only the
one that matches and silently skips the rest. Next.js already does this for
@next/swc, which is why that package alone worked on both platforms.
Versions must track @tailwindcss/oxide and the lightningcss under
@tailwindcss/node. `npm run check:toolchain` fails when they drift, and CI
runs it — so a Tailwind bump that forgets these is caught, even though CI
runs on Linux and cannot see a missing win32 binary directly.
